parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a national document/entry regime (sex locked to M/F at conception, X markers barred, discrepancy → refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, passports blocked leaving travelers stranded) onto a state with no gender-identity discrimination statute, a hate-crime law excluding gender identity, birth-certificate markers closed, facility-use restriction in state buildings, and a felony-level bar on minor gender-affirming care. Outing follows every ID check. Mitigants are real but partial: national employment and hate-crime coverage, functioning courts enjoining several orders, legal-aid guidance, 78% public support for non-discrimination, and no documented state violence incident. Worst documented outcome is arrest/denial, not imprisonment-likely.

entry_documents.exposure: National order locks passport/visa sex to assigned sex at birth; X markers barred (Feb 2025); Feb 2025 cable orders refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and invites lifetime fraud-ineligibility analysis; travelers report passports blocked/stranded abroad; state birth-certificate markers closed, forcing disclosure when documents are shown.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; suit by civil-liberties union pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: State document closure compounds the federal entry regime: no state route to align records, so any ID check (hotel, police, clinic) re-exposes the traveler to federal mismatch scrutiny.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopts conversion-therapy-style inmate policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; state facility laws invite trespass enforcement; one state arrest precedent shows 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Fraud charges not automatic; courts have enjoined several executive orders; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document mismatch or facility dispute can escalate into custody where birth-sex placement and the rescinded prison-respect policy apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State's April 2023 law explicitly allows restricting trans people's bathroom usage in many state-run facilities; national order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; equality map shows widening subnational bans, 4 states with criminal triggers.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented state criminal facility statute in this state; exemptions modelled in comparable statutes (emergency, chaperoning, out-of-order).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a courthouse, rest area or capitol restroom risks removal and trespass referral under state rule plus federal-facility exclusion.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors illegal in-state since 2023 (veto-proof); federal orders frame minor care as mutilation and direct prosecution of facilitators; proposed national rules bar insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Conversion therapy banned for state social workers/psychologists (2021); several federal orders blocked or enjoined; adult care not documented as banned.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, potential guardian scrutiny and record exposure; adult HRT continuity is an open question, not a documented ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animi; executive orders direct law-enforcement investigation of 'gender ideology' in schools; advocates compare trajectory to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward criterion never names gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability and severity of any discretionary encounter, amplifying document and facility exposures.

minors_guardians.exposure: In-state minor care banned; May 2023 law requires disclosure of transgender students to parents in state schools; 2023 student bill carries penalty provisions; federal order threatens prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: School provisions concern state-run schools, not short-term visitors; national employment and hate-crime protections extend to families; no documented enforcement against visiting guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family seeking any state service or school-adjacent contact can trigger inquiry, care refusal, or separation of the child from support.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity; no state anti-discrimination statute; 2021 law lets student groups discriminate against LGBT students; party platform rhetoric accused trans people of preying on women.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity (2009); national employment ruling (2020); no dated trans violence incident in state sources; 2022 poll shows 78% support for LGBTQ non-discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of incident data is not safety, but public support plus federal coverage gives a visitor real, if uneven, recourse after street hostility.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Many federal orders unresolved or inconsistently in force; final disposition of the 2023 religious-refusal bill unknown; relationship between 2008 and 2008/2023 birth-certificate rules unclear; no documented enforcement of the student-bill penalty.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning federal courts have enjoined multiple measures; civil-liberties litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained; city-level protections exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work for those who reach them, but the operative rule at any moment varies by forum, leaving exposure unpredictable rather than absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above 0.15-B: no border detention regime, no crowd cells, no withheld medical care in custody, no credible capital pathway, and courts actively enjoin federal measures. Document friction here is administrative refusal and outing, not prolonged custody with failing remedies.

Above 0.35-C: no universal lodging-reporting or eviction-and-fund-freeze regime. Exposure is mismatch scrutiny and service denial under a state with no GI public-accommodation law, plus facility and minor-care bars — broader in kind but without a systematic shelter-loss apparatus.

Close to 0.45-B: like it, visitor-facing exclusions are concentrated in education and health for minors, remedies are limited to apologies or litigation, enforcement varies, and imprisonment for the visitor is atypical; federal document rules add a continuous outing exposure that anchor lacks.

Below 0.55-B: unlike that anchor's respectful trained border staff and appeal desk, here officers are instructed to refuse on sex discrepancy with a lifetime-ineligibility option; state facility restriction and minor-care felony push severity above discretionary secondary screening.

Well below 0.85-C: care protections, ombuds enforcement and licensing discipline are absent for state visitors; in-state minor care is criminalised and facility access is restrictable, whereas that anchor documents remedies that function in practice.

parsed.synthesis: The traveler faces one continuous federal exposure (sex-locked documents, X-marker ban, refusal-and-fraud screening) layered on a state that closes birth-certificate markers, omits gender-identity discrimination and hate-crime coverage, permits facility exclusion in state buildings, and criminalises minor gender-affirming care. Each ID check, restroom, or clinic visit re-triggers outing with the state powerless to align records. Severity stops short of imprisonment: worst documented outcomes are arrest, service denial, entry refusal and care denial. Real mitigation exists — federal employment and hate-crime coverage, courts enjoining orders, legal-aid guidance, 78% public support, two-spirit traditions — but it operates in litigation, not at the counter. Adults alone sit mid-scale; a family with a trans minor is materially worse because care is banned and disclosure duties attach.
